name: India

nso.name: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India (ORGI), Ministry of Home Affairs

latest_census.notes: 2011 is the last completed census: religion (table C-01), mother tongue (C-16) and Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe status (incl. individual tribe, ST tables) were asked and published down to district and sub-district; no ethnicity question. The 2021 round was never held. Census 2027 is now scheduled: search results (Republic World 2026-08-14, Open magazine, Deccan Herald) say the MHA has notified a 40-question Population Enumeration schedule that asks religion, 'Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe status or caste' (the first full caste enumeration since 1931), mother tongue and other languages known; Houselisting runs April-September 2026 and Population Enumeration in February 2027. Nothing from 2027 is publishable before the tabulations appear, so 2011 remains the source of record for now.

subnational_sources.format: xls (one workbook per state; direct download links exist, e.g. https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/11382/download/14495/DDW27C-01%20MDDS.XLS for Maharashtra)
subnational_sources.evidence: Search results list catalogue entries PC11_C01-00 (India, 11361) and per-state entries: Punjab 11389, Assam 11365, West Bengal 11396, Sikkim 11391, Bihar 11366, Maharashtra 11382, plus the C-01 Appendix (11398) and Annexure (11397) that itemise the 'Other religions and persuasions' residual. The catalogue IDs for C-01 are contiguous (11361-11398), and a direct /download/ URL surfaced, so the 'cannot be automated' verdict in docs/SOURCES.md may be worth re-measuring from the runner.

It does not overturn the packet's not_collected declaration for ethnicity: India counts SC/ST status and individual tribe names, not ethnicity, and ST-14 would need ~640 downloads to assemble. Recorded so the next person knows the closest official table exists and what it is.

tier_reason: Census 2011 counts religion (C-01) and mother tongue (C-16) and publishes both by district in XLS/CSV; the repo already fills 35/36 states and 637/735 districts from them. The new finding is an official keyless CSV/XLS of C-01 on data.gov.in that can replace the community GitHub extract as the retrieval path, plus evidence that NADA exposes direct /download/ URLs.
recommended_action: 1) Point india_census.py at the data.gov.in resource (or the NADA per-state XLS via the contiguous catalogue IDs 11361-11398) so the 2011 religion figures come from an official path; values should reproduce NATIONAL_CONTROLS exactly, so this is a provenance change, not a data change -- owner review only. 2) Keep ethnicity declared not_collected; ST-14 is an ST-by-religion cross-tab, not an ethnic composition. 3) Nothing to do for language: C-16 is built. 4) Diary Census 2027 (enumeration February 2027; caste, religion and mother tongue all asked) -- tabulations will take years; re-check censusindia.gov.in from 2028. 5) Run the three admin2 Wikipedia sample searches that could not be run here.

summary: India's source of record is still Census 2011: religion (C-01) and mother tongue (C-16) were counted and published by state, district and sub-district, and the repo already fills 35/36 states and 637/735 districts from them; the 98 empty districts are post-2011 creations. The genuinely new finding is that the official C-01 table sits on data.gov.in as an OGD resource with state/district/tehsil codes (and per-state copies), and that the NADA catalogue exposes direct /download/ XLS URLs with contiguous IDs 11361-11398 -- either would replace the community GitHub CSV with an official retrieval path for the same numbers. Ethnicity remains legitimately not_collected; the nearest official table is ST-14 (Scheduled Tribe by religion, one XLS per district), a legal-category cross-tab rather than a composition. Census 2027 (enumeration February 2027) will ask religion, caste and mother tongue, but nothing from it is publishable yet. The three admin2 Wikipedia sample checks were not run because the session's search budget ran out.
